_comment: Registry of off-the-shelf MCP servers the on-device agent can borrow.
Each entry is a config dict for harness/mcp_bridge.enable(), plus three
These are THIRD-PARTY servers. They hold your OAuth tokens, not us. See
README.md in this folder for what that means and for the migration path to

selftest.summary: Fake mailbox for testing the wiring. No credentials, no network.
setup: Nothing to set up. Verifies the bridge on a fresh machine:
python3 agents/8b/run_agent.py --mcp selftest --mcp-list
Draft mode should expose list/read/draft/modify and DROP send/reply/login.

gmail.summary: Gmail — read/search mail, create drafts. Draft mode drops send_email.
setup: Create an OAuth client (Desktop app) in Google Cloud, enable the Gmail API.
Save the client JSON as ~/.gmail-mcp/gcp-oauth.keys.json
Run once, interactively:  npx @gongrzhe/server-gmail-autoauth-mcp auth
That writes ~/.gmail-mcp/credentials.json, which the server reuses.
NOTE: this repo was archived March 2026 — still functional, but unmaintained.
It is the first candidate to replace with a first-party server.
notes: write_tools exists because the bridge's name-based classifier misses
'modify_*' — it has no write verb in _WRITE_RE, so without this override
modify_email would be exposed as read-only and skip confirmation.
download_attachment writes to local disk, so it is a write too.

gcal.summary: Google Calendar — list/search events, free-busy, create and update events.
setup: Reuse the same Google Cloud OAuth client as gmail, and enable the Calendar API.
Point GOOGLE_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS at the client JSON (see env below).
First run opens a browser for consent and caches the token.

ms365.summary: Outlook mail + calendar via Microsoft Graph. Draft mode drops send-mail.
setup: Run once, interactively, and call its 'login' tool to do the device-code flow:
npx @softeria/ms-365-mcp-server --preset mail,calendar
The token cache is reused after that, so the agent never sees the login.
Optional: set MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID / MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID to use your own
Azure app registration instead of the server's built-in public client.
notes: Measured, not guessed: `--mcp ms365 --mcp-list` against the real server
returns 69 tools even with --preset mail,calendar. That is far past what
an 8B can hold in an 8k context, so the allow list above cuts it to ten.
Widen it from the --mcp-list output, never from memory.
login/logout are dropped because the classifier reads them as harmless
(no write verb), which would let the model trigger a blocking device-code
prompt mid-run. A human logs in out of band; the agent never should.
The three write_tools are real classifier misses found in that same run:
copy/dismiss/snooze all change state but contain no verb _WRITE_RE knows,
so without the override they would run without asking. get-mailbox-settings
is the opposite — it matches 'set' inside 'settings' and is only a read.

ms365-personal.summary: Outlook mail + calendar for a PERSONAL account (outlook.com/hotmail).
setup: Log in once with the same authority the agent will use:
MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID=consumers npx @softeria/ms-365-mcp-server --login --preset mail,calendar
Then enter the code at https://www.microsoft.com/link (NOT login.microsoft.com/device).
Do NOT trust --verify-login: it reports 'Silent token acquisition failed'
even when the connection is fine. Test with a real call instead:
python3 agents/8b/run_agent.py --mcp ms365-personal --mcp-list
notes: Use this, not 'ms365', for a personal Microsoft account. The server's own
auth.js carries the reason: as of June 2026 Microsoft rejects tokens issued
to personal accounts through the default 'common' authority, so the tenant
must be pinned to 'consumers'. Symptom if you get it wrong: the device page
bounces to localhost/callback with a missing 'response_type' error and no
token is ever cached.
The authority must match between login and runtime — hence the env here.

teams.summary: Microsoft Teams chat — list chats, read messages. Posting needs --live.
setup: Same server and same login as ms365, with --org-mode for work/school features.
Requires a work/school account; a personal Microsoft account has no Teams.
If your tenant restricts the server's built-in app, register your own Azure
app and set MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID / MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID — this usually needs
a tenant admin to consent to the Chat.* delegated scopes.
notes: IN DRAFT MODE THIS IS READ-ONLY. Teams has no concept of a draft, so every
way to put a message in front of a person is a transmit tool and the bridge
drops all of them. Reading chats works; posting needs --mcp-live.
Running this alongside 'ms365' starts a second copy of the same server.
Use 'ms365-work' instead to get mail + calendar + teams in one process.

ms365-work.summary: One server covering Outlook mail, calendar and Teams chat (work account).
setup: Same login as ms365. Use this INSTEAD OF ms365 + teams, not alongside them.
notes: No allow list here on purpose — this preset spans three surfaces, so run
`--mcp ms365-work --mcp-list` against your own tenant and narrow it to the
tools you actually demo. Unfiltered it is well over 100 tools.
